messages:
sofia_customer: Hey, we’re seeing the chat stream drop the final ~200 tokens intermittently (client only gets prefix + mid-chunk, then stream ends). Happens with SSE to our frontend. Request ID: req_0b12c9a4. Example curl we used: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.test/v1/chat/stream" -d "{\"model\":\"redwood-XX\",\"messages\":...}\"` — attaching server-side logs shortly.

maria_support: Thanks @sofia_customer — we’ll triage. Do you have a minimal repro we can run locally? Also, is this behind any CDN/proxy (Fastly/Cloudflare) or an internal edge? Any client library (EventSource, fetch/ReadableStream, websocket shim)?

sofia_customer: Frontend uses EventSource polyfill (legacy FF) + our nginx reverse proxy in front of the app. We see this on chrome sometimes too. I can reproduce with a simple Node curl from our app server. Proxy config: keepalive 60s, chunked transfer enabled. No obvious errors in nginx logs.

ajay_eng-runtime: @sofia_customer can you paste the exact curl you used and the raw response headers/first/last bytes (hexdump or base64)? If possible include the SSE payload chunk boundaries (lines with `data:`). Also include the response Content-Length (if any) and Transfer-Encoding.

sofia_customer: pasted curl below and raw capture (trimmed):
```
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.test/v1/chat/stream" -d '{"model":"redwood-xx","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
Response headers:
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-request-id: req_0b12c9a4
```
First SSE chunk (ok): `data: {"delta":"Hello","role":"assistant"}\n\n`
Later chunk (truncated): `data: {"delta":"...last partial token"` (no closing `}\n\n`)

maria_support: That truncation looks like a client-side buffer flush failure or a proxy coalescing issue. @evan_eng-sre can you check edge traces for req_0b12c9a4? Also @sofia_customer, please run `ngrep -W byline host api.redwood.test and port 443` (or tcpdump if you can) while reproducing to capture the final TLS record boundaries.

evan_eng-sre: I pulled the edge logs for req_0b12c9a4 — upstream returned 200 with chunked encoding, no obvious 502/timeout. I’m requesting the backend service logs from runtime team (linking deploy-bot).

deploy-bot: runtime-service: new logs available for req_0b12c9a4 -> /var/log/runtime/2026/03/17/req_0b12c9a4.log

ajay_eng-runtime: Thanks. Two concrete asks to narrow root cause:
1) Sofia — please produce a minimal curl that includes `--no-buffer` and `--raw` flags to avoid client buffering, e.g. `curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.test/v1/chat/stream` and paste the exact terminal output (raw bytes if possible).
2) If you can reproduce reliably, send us a HAR or a pcap of the failing session. If pcap is sensitive, a `tcpdump -w /tmp/session.pcap host api.redwood.test and port 443` and upload via our debug upload link.

sofia_customer: Ok running now with `--no-buffer`. Initial result: still saw one truncated event. I uploaded `session.pcap` to the debug bucket: s3://redwood-debug/sofia/1933334444-session.pcap

ajay_eng-runtime: Got the pcap, thanks. Quick notes after initial glance: last TLS record from server shows 1.2KB payload then connection close from client side immediately after. That suggests the client closed before full SSE event flush, possibly due to EventSource polyfill bug where it stops reading on CRLF patterns. Can you confirm your client cancels the connection programmatically on certain UI actions? Also paste the client console logs (network tab) for the time of the repro.

sofia_customer: We don't cancel programmatically. Console shows `EventSource error` at same time. We'll try to reproduce with raw fetch + ReadableStream to rule out EventSource behavior.

maria_support: One more thing — please include the runtime `redwood-request-id` header value if present (different from x-request-id), and any server-side stacktrace or stderr lines around the request. If you can’t find them, we’ll pull the full debug bundle from the runtime logs we linked earlier.

sofia_customer: Found `redwood-request-id: r-7f5c3b`. I attached the last 30 lines of runtime stderr in the upload: s3://redwood-debug/sofia/1933334444-runtime-tail.log

evan_eng-sre: Review complete — stderr shows a `client disconnect` on the runtime at the exact timestamp when the SSE event was partial. Two possibilities: (1) intermediate proxy/nginx on customer side closing socket on parse error, (2) client EventSource polyfill giving up. For next repro, try bypassing your nginx (call API directly from a simple VM) and reproduce. If it still fails, we escalate to networking & kernel-level collection (we'll need a pcap on both sides and the nginx config).

sofia_customer: Bypassed nginx — I reproduced straight from VM using curl --no-buffer and still got truncated final event. Uploading new pcap to same bucket: s3://redwood-debug/sofia/1933334444-bypassed.pcap

ajay_eng-runtime: Since it reproduces without customer proxy, this suggests a server-side flush issue or a kernel-level TLS send being cut by our runtime when closing the stream. I'll instrument the runtime to log `write()` sizes and flush boundaries for the next rollout. Meanwhile we'll keep monitoring and I’ll follow up once we have those logs. If you need an ETA for a patch, say so and we’ll prioritize.

sofia_customer: ETA would be great — production users are seeing occasional message loss. Anything temporary we can do? (retries, client-side heuristics)

maria_support: Short-term mitigation: client should treat incomplete JSON in SSE `data:` as transient and attempt to re-open stream or buffer until `\n\n` boundary appears. We'll provide a small client wrapper snippet for resilient SSE consumption. Engineering will update when runtime write/flush logs are available.

ajay_eng-runtime: Noted — I’ll push instrumentation and tag the rollout with `fix/sse-flush-logging`. I’ll paste the additional logs here when available and link to a follow-up thread with the RCA. Thanks everyone for the fast help. :thumbsup:
